title: decision(gates): should the cross-file citation parser's proximity window widen from 2 to 5 — measured at +14 rows, 11 of them real citations
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:spec@objectui` PM seat, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`, out of the residue of objectui#9026 (PR objectui#9082). ⛔ Not claimed. ⛔ No `domain:*` or `priority:*` applied — routing and grading are triage's.

## The decision

`scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` scopes a bare `:NNN` continuation address to within **2 lines** of an address already in scope. objectui#9026 taught the parser to see the continuation form at all; it deliberately **did not touch that window**, and this card carries the one question that change left open.

**Should the window widen from 2 to 5?**

## Why this is a real question and not a loose end

⭐ The cost is already **measured**, which is the whole reason it is worth a card rather than a comment. Widening to 5 — the smallest width that reaches the case that motivated it — costs **+14 rows** tree-wide:

| newly visible at window 5 | count |
|---|---|
| real cross-file line citations | **11** |
| a port number in prose | 1 |
| a cron minute | 1 |
| a Chinese enumeration | 1 |

⇒ 11 real against 3 false. That ratio is defensible, and it is exactly the trade the window exists to make — so this is a judgement about where to sit on it, ⛔ not a defect.

A third option was measured and **refuted on its numbers**: scoping by prose paragraph instead of line count reaches all six addresses but costs **+49** rows, mostly JSON object literals and ports.

## ⭐ What is already settled, so nobody re-derives it

**The window is deliberate and it was not the cause of objectui#9026's blindness.** Measured on that card: with the continuation trigger absent and the window widened to **999999**, the six-address docblock still read **0 of 6**. ⇒ ⛔ do not re-open this as "the window was the bug" — it was not, and objectui#9026's fix is independent of whatever is decided here.

## The concrete case

One address of the six that motivated objectui#9026 stays out of scope at window 2: it is restated in a second paragraph, eight lines below the only filename and carrying none of its own. It is **pinned as blind by name** in `scripts/__tests__/cross-file-line-citation-census.test.ts`, with the cost of reaching it recorded there — so today it is a **declared** gap rather than a silent one, which is the state objectui#9026 existed to reach.

⇒ ⚠️ Nothing here is red. The gate is report-only, the blindness is declared, and a seat is free to close this card by ruling "window stays at 2" — that is a legitimate outcome, not a non-answer.

## ⚠️ Not measured

- Whether any of the 11 newly-visible real citations have **rotted** (objectui#9026 measured the population and the false count tree-wide, ⛔ not this subset).
- Whether widths between 2 and 5 reach the motivating case at a lower cost — only 2, 5 and paragraph-scope were measured.
- Whether the 3 false rows could be excluded structurally. ⚠️ On the adjacent population this was tried and every structural filter that removed ports and JSON literals **also removed real citations**, so assume that generalises until someone shows otherwise.

Refs objectui#9026 (the parser change and every measurement above) · objectui#9082 (the PR) · objectui#9081 (a separate census defect found in the same work).
